2026-09-04.part1: Friday closed the week with gold carrying the tape. MNQ moved 0.14% on a 236.5 point range, just 0.55x median: a quiet session ahead of the jobs report. MGC closed down 0.63% but its range ran 126.5 points, 1.39x median, wide enough on its own to mark the day mattered. Six gold headlines ran, most pointing to eased hawkish Fed bets and a push back toward $4,500, with one asking whether the metal could break higher. It did not: the close came in lower, not higher. The intraday swings back that story up. The close does not. Two Nasdaq stories flagged futures edging higher into the jobs number, and Nasdaq obliged by doing almost nothing. A busy print run, a flat tape.
2026-09-04.part2: The week mattered four sessions out of five, Wednesday the exception. Monday moved on gold: MGC down 1.07% as Iran conflict and Fed rate hike stories ran alongside a flat Nasdaq. Tuesday was the week's big print, MNQ down 1.31% and MGC down 1.89%, both tagged mattered, as $91 to $95 oil, surging bond yields and dollar strength drove the sharpest closes of the week. Wednesday was the loud one that changed nothing: three headlines called Nasdaq futures slipping, and MNQ closed up 0.21%; four gold headlines flagged weakness below $4,300, and MGC closed up 0.41%. Thursday reversed hard, MGC up 2.84% on a Fed voter list and a softer dollar, MNQ up 1.16% on Broadcom-linked megacap headlines. Friday's forecasts of a $4,500 breakout closed lower, though gold's wide range alone tagged the day mattered. The week's lesson: the loudest headlines ran opposite the close more than once, and volume of coverage told you nothing about direction.
